full_judgment:
Abdul Bari Sarker, J.: This application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure is for quashing the proceeding of Case No. 56 of 1990 under Section 4 of the Dowary Prohibition Act; 1980 pending in the Court of the Upazilla Magistrate, Sherajdikhan, District—Munshiganj. 

 2. The prosecution case as appears from the Petition of Complaint Annexure-A is that on 15.2.90 at about 10 A.M. accused No. 1 Md. Mohiuddin Chokder, husband of the complainant Opposite-Party No. 2 at the instigations of the other three accused persons including the petitioner Anowara Begum demanded dowry of Taka 50,000/- from the complainant opposite party No. 2 Shahida Begum but as she expressed the inability of her father to pay so much money, the accused persons allegedly assaulted her. 

 4. Mr. Alaluddin, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that the petition of complainant does not disclose any offence as contemplated under Section 4 of the Dowary Prohibition Act, 1980, as the alleged demand for dowry, even if assumed to be true, does not come within the mischief of 'dowry' as given in the definition of dowry in Section 2 of the same Act. In support of his contention, he refer to and relies on the case of Mihir Lal Saha Poddar @ Mihir Kumar Poddar, Motilal Saha Poddar, Petitioners Vs. Zhunu Rani Saha, Opposite party, reported in 37 D.L.R. at page 227, Where it was held that "property to be given or agreed to be given as consideration for marriage in order to call it a dowry." 

 in Section 2 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1980, it is clear that the payment must be "as a consideration for the marriage" to be considered as a dowry. In the present case, from the petition of complaint, it is clear that the claim for dowry was made long after the marriage and not as a consideration for marriage. The claim for dowry in the present case does not come with in the mischief of the definition of dowry given in Section 2 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1980. 

 7. The Learned Advocate for the petitioner further submits that the learned Magistrate issued summons against the accused persons without examining the complainant as required under Section 200 Cr.P.C. and as such, the case is liable to be quashed. In support of his contention he refers to and relies on the decision and also the decision made in the case of Alauddin Ahmed-petitioner Vs. State, Naresh Chandra Kundu-Opposite parties; reported in 20 D.L.R. at page 590. In the case of Mihir Lal Saha, Poddar, it was held as follows: 

 In the other case, it was held that order of inquiry without examining of complainant is illegal. 

 9. In the result, the revisional application is allowed. The impugned proceeding of Case No. 59(e) of 1990 is hereby quashed and the Rule is made absolute.
